headline: Approved parking permits for 488-494 Dexter Street and parking variances for 42-44 West Hunt Street; denied open-area variance at 40-42 Fletcher Street.
summary: Approved a parking permit with conditions for 488-494 Dexter Street and two parking aisle width variances for 42-44 West Hunt Street. Denied a lot open area variance for 40-42 Fletcher Street after staff recommended denial. Continued the 319 Hunt Street request to the next meeting.
decisions: Continued approval of the July 22, 2026 minutes to the next meeting.
Continued the variance request for 319 Hunt Street to the next regularly scheduled meeting, passed unanimously by voice vote.
Approved special-use permits for 488-494 Dexter Street with the conditions outlined by staff, passed unanimously by voice vote.
Approved a dimensional variance of four feet from the parking aisle width requirement for the northerly garage at 42-44 West Hunt Street, passed unanimously by voice vote.
Approved a dimensional variance of four feet from the parking aisle width requirement for the southerly garage at 42-44 West Hunt Street, passed unanimously by voice vote.
Denied the request for a dimensional variance from the lot open area requirement at 40-42 Fletcher Street, passed unanimously by voice vote.

plain_text:
CITY OF CENTRAL FALLS 
                 COMBINED PLANNING AND ZONING BOARD 
 
 
Page 1 of 5 
REGULAR MEETING 
(PUBLIC HEARING) 
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 6:00 PM 
The Bessette Building (DPW) – 1280 High Street, Central Falls, RI 02863 
 
MINUTES 
I. Call to Order 
Chair Marenzana called the meeting to order at 6:01 PM. 
II. Roll Call 
Chair Marenzana called the roll and the following members were present: John Marenzana, Hugo  
Figueroa, Dan Klotz, Ann Peckham, and Kevin Marchand. Also in attendance were:  Joshua B. Magnone, 
Principal Deputy Director for Planning, and Joseph P. Baxter, Legal Counsel. 
III. Pledge of Allegiance 
Chair Marenzana led the Board in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance.  
IV. Approval of Minutes 
A.  Regular Meeting Minutes of July 22, 2026 
Mr. Magnone requested that approval of the minutes be continued to the next meeting. There was no 
objection. 
V. Public Comment 
Chair Marenzana opened the floor to public comment. 
Mr. Magnone stated that there were no names listed on the sign-up sheet. 
VI. New Business 
Mr. Magnone stated that the Applicant for 319 Hunt Street wished to request a continuance and 
requested that its application be taken out of order as the first item. Mr.  Figueroa moved the motion, 
seconded by Ms. Peckham. The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. 
There was no objection, the motion passed unanimously. 
B.  Pursuant to its local and statutory authority as the Zoning Board, discussion and possible votes on 
      Application PZB-2026-09Z: 
Effuahson, LLC, of 40 Toronto Avenue, Providence, RI, represented by Jones Harris, Applicant 
for 319 Hunt Street (Assessor's Plat 3, Lot 121), proposes to construct an addition to the 
existing principal garage. The Applicant seeks a Use Variance to expand the legal 
nonconforming use and Dimensional Variances from rear-yard setback requirements (Art. IV, 
Sec. 401, R-3 Zone), maximum lot coverage requirements (Art. IV, Sec. 401, R -3 Zone), and 
from the requirements of Art. IV, Sec. 401.1(B) to permit a total open area of less than 800 
square feet on the subject property.
Page 2 of 5 
The Applicant’s agent, Jones Harris, appeared before the Board. Mr. Harris requested a continuance 
due to the inability for his attorney and expert witness to attend the public hearing. 
Mr. Marchand motioned to continue the mater to the next regularly scheduled meeting, seconded by 
Ms. Peckham. The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There was no 
objection, the motion passed unanimously. 
A.  Pursuant to its local and statutory authority as the Zoning Board, discussion and possible votes on 
      Application PZB-2026-08Z: 
Juan Rodriguez, of 901 Roosevelt Ave, Pawtucket, RI, Applicant for 488 -494 Dexter Street 
(Plat 6, Lot 344) seeks Special-Use Permits to provide fewer than the minimum number of off-
street parking spaces required and to provide off-site parking (Art. V, Sec. 514.13(b)-(c)). 
The Applicant, Juan Rodriguez, and the son of the property owner, Octavio Munoz, appeared before 
the Board. Both were sworn in by Attorney Baxter. 
Mr. Rodriguez explained his request to the Board regarding reduced parking during outdoor events 
held in the on -site parking lot. He also described an outdoor screen that he proposes to use for 
entertainment during events and as a sign during non-event periods. 
Mr. Rodriguez explained further that he surveyed the nearby street and identified 45 on-street parking 
spaces. 
Mr. Figueroa asked how many parking spaces are located on the subject property. Mr. Rodriguez 
explained that he provides approximately eight or nine parking spaces. Referring to an aerial image, 
Mr. Magnone stated that he believes there are approximately 11 or 12 parking spaces, although some 
may be obstructed by an outdoor tent shown in the image. 
Chair Marenzana asked about the size of the outdoor screen mentioned by Mr. Rodriguez. Mr. 
Magnone responded that the screen was not included on the agenda for discussion. Further, that the 
Fire Department had previously raised a concern regarding the screen blocking windows, which has 
since been corrected by lowering the screen. According to Mr. Magnone, he has not been informed 
by the Zoning Official that the screen is nonconforming. 
Mr. Magnone requested that the Staff Memorandum for 488 -494 Dexter Street be entered into the 
record as “Exhibit A.” Mr.  Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Ms. Peckham. The vote was 
taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There was no objection, the motion passed 
unanimously. 
Mr. Magnone presented the Staff Memorandum to the Board regarding the Applicant’s request for a 
special use permit. He stated that the Planning Department is not opposed to the Applicant’s request; 
however, he recommended that, if approved, the special use permit be subject to certain conditions. 
Mr. Klotz left the meeting to use the restroom. 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to approve the Applicant’s application with the conditions 
outlined by Mr. Magnone. Mr. Figueroa moved the motion, seconded by Mr. Marchand. The vote was 
taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There was no objection, the motion passed 
unanimously. 
Mr. Klotz returned from the restroom and asked that his vote be recorded in the affirmative. 
C.  Pursuant to its local and statutory authority as the Zoning Board, discussion and possible votes on 
      Application PZB-2026-10Z: 
Elie Osko, of 6 Cook Street, Lincoln, RI, Owner and Applicant for 42-44 West Hunt Street (Plat 
7, Lot 123), proposes to construct a 2 -story addition to the existing principal residence. The
Page 3 of 5 
Applicant seeks Dimensional Variances from minimum parking aisle width requirements (Art. 
VIII, Sec. 801.2, 90-Degree Angle). 
Attorney Baxter swore in Zack Kelling, of Level Design Group, appearing on behalf of the Applicant. 
Mr. Kelling provided a summary of the proposal and of the relief requested. 
Mr. Marchand inquired about the nature of the addition, Mr. Kelling responded that it was a two-unit 
addition at the rear of the existing building. 
The Applicant, Mr. Osko, also appeared before the Board and summarized the proposal and 
requested relief. Mr. Osko added that they added green space on the side of the addition, which 
further necessitated this relief. 
Mr. Marchand raised concerns of whether vehicles would have to back out onto West Hunt Street. 
Mr. Kelling stated the turning analysis concluded that vehicles would have plenty of room to pull up 
and into the garages with the requested aisle width. 
Mr. Marchand asked if an emergency vehicle could access the back of the property, Mr. Osko 
responded that there is plenty of room. 
Mr. Magnone requested that the Staff Memorandum for 42 -44 West Hunt Street be entered into the 
record as “Exhibit B .” Mr.  Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Ms. Peckham. The vote was 
taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There was no objection, the motion passed 
unanimously. 
Mr. Magnone presented the Staff Memorandum to the Board regarding the Applicant’s request for 
dimensional variances. He stated that the Planning Department is not opposed to the Applicant’s 
request and discussed the reasoning provided in the Memorandum. 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to approve the Applicant’s request for a dimensional variance 
from the parking aisle width requirements applicable to the R-3 Zone, as set forth in Article IV, Section 
401 of the Zoning Ordinance, specifically, relief of four (4) feet from the re quired parking aisle width 
in relation to the garage at the northerly portion of the proposed structure. Mr. Marchand moved the 
motion, seconded by Mr. Figueroa. The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the 
affirmative. There was no objection, the motion passed unanimously. 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to approve the Applicant’s request for a dimensional variance 
from the parking aisle width requirements applicable to the R-3 Zone, as set forth in Article IV, Section 
401 of the Zoning Ordinance, specifically, relief of four (4) feet from the re quired parking aisle width 
in relation to the garage at the southerly portion of the proposed structure. Mr. Figueroa moved the 
motion, seconded by Ms. Peckham . The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the 
affirmative. There was no objection, the motion passed unanimously. 
Mr. Osko thanked the Board. 
D.  Pursuant to its local and statutory authority as the Zoning Board, discussion and possible votes on 
      Application PZB-2026-11Z: 
Balwant Sandhu, of 4 Bartlett Road, Methuen, MA, Owner and Applicant for 40 -42 Fletcher 
Street (Plat 5, Lot 301) seeks a Dimensional Variance from the requirements of Art. IV, Sec. 
401.1(B), to permit a total open area of less than 800 square feet on the subject property. 
The Applicant, Balwant Sandhu, and his son, Jaskaran Singh, appeared before the Board. 
Both Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Singh were sworn in by Attorney Baxter.
Page 4 of 5 
Mr. Sandhu provided a summary of their request for relief, including that the Department of Health 
found lead on the property, the soil was paved over to remediate lead in the soil, and the property 
received a conditional lead certificate. 
Mr. Magnone provided the Planning Department’s summary of facts, including that a City inspector 
noticed that the entirety of the property was paved, which resulted in a notice of zoning violation for 
lack of sufficient permeable space.  
Mr. Magnone stated that Mr. Sandhu, upon receiving the notice of violation, was very responsive and 
then promptly filed for the requested relief. 
Mr. Magnone continued by stating that the hardship for which the Applicant seeks relief resulted from 
a prior action of the Applicant, a factor on which the Board is required to make a positive finding. For 
this reason, along with the other negative findings identified in the staff memorandum and the 
potential availability of alternative means to mitigate the lead condition in a manner that complies with 
zoning requirements, Mr. Magnone recommended that the Board deny the Applicant’s request for 
relief. 
Mr. Marchand stated the Applicant’s dilemma is a “double-sword,” as he was told to cover the lead by 
the State Department of Health, but the City is telling him that he’s covered too much. 
Mr. Magnone acknowledged the dilemma but highlighted that there are means of covering the lead, 
while also retaining enough permeable surface to meet the City’s zoning requirements. 
Ms. Peckham  mentioned that she previously owned property where she abated lead in  a similar 
manner and questioned whether the ordinance had changed. 
Mr. Marchand asked if a French drain could be installed. 
Mr. Magnone mentioned that he  believes the zoning ordinance does not contemplate  using 
techniques like that and suggested that the ordinance could be amended in the future. Further adding 
that the current requirement is minimal and should be made proportional to properties in the future. 
Mr. Magnone commented that, due to the Applicant’s responsiveness, he anticipates that the Zoning 
Official will work with the Applicant to find an agreeable solution, as opposed leading with fines. 
Mr. Magnone and the Applicant discussed potential mitigation options. 
Chair Marenzana stated his understanding of the matter. 
Mr. Sandhu stated that they purchased the property with five lead hazard certificates. Further stating 
that by incapsulating the lead with the asphalt, they do not run the risk of testing positive again. 
Chair Marenzana inquired as to whether the Applicant kn ew of the City ’s intention to oppose his 
request ahead of the meeting. 
Mr. Magnone responded that all Applicant’s receive the staff report prior to the meeting. 
Mr. Magnone reiterated Planning’s position  that the Applicant does not sa tisfy the applicable 
standards for relief and that there are alternative methods to  mitigate the lead th at sa tisfy zoning 
requirements. 
Chair Marenzana asked if the State submits paperwork to the City when they confirm the presence of 
lead on a property. 
Mr. Magnone responded that he is unsure but presumes that they do notify the City. 
Mr. Sandhu stated that any permeable space on the property will likely lead to future lead violations 
and would disqualify the property from a full lead-safe certificate.
Page 5 of 5 
Mr. Marenzana asked if the Board has any further questions. 
Mr. Marchand stated that the State should explain the full range of mitigation options to lead violators. 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to deny the Applicant’s request for a dimensional variance from 
the minimum lot open area requirements set forth in Article IV, Section 401.1(B) of the Zoning 
Ordinance, specifically, relief of 800 square feet from the required minimum lot open area.  Mr. 
Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Mr. Klotz. The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members 
voted in the affirmative. There was no objection, the motion passed unanimously. 
Mr. Magnone and Mr. Sandhu discussed next steps and getting in-touch with the Zoning Official. 
VII. Adjournment 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to adjourn. Mr. Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Mr. 
Klotz. The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There was no objection, 
the motion passed unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 7:06 PM.
